deviations_from_adr: ADR §2.6/§4 D2 preferred importing the compiled core module into the web bundle, with a shared-copy fallback under fitness-parity ('шаренная копия под fitness-паритетом'). The literal pattern the ADR text implies (a `.js`-suffixed import specifier resolving the sibling `.ts` source, as commented in web/src/forms/Floor2Viewer.jsx) does NOT actually resolve under this repo's vite/vitest toolchain — verified empirically (a `.js`-suffixed import of src/core/formula-parser.js failed with 'Cannot find module' under both `vitest run` and `vite build`; FormDocumentRenderer.test.jsx's own comment independently confirms the Floor2Viewer.jsx import is a 'build-only twin' its unit tests deliberately keep off the test module graph for the same reason). The ACTUAL working pattern was already established in this exact file's own test (apps-schema.test.js imports `../../../src/core/record-schema-validator.ts` with the explicit `.ts` extension) — switching apps-schema.js and records-form.js to that pattern resolves correctly in both vitest and the production `vite build`. This is the STRONGER form of the ADR's own preference (one true source, zero copy, zero parity-check surface to maintain) rather than a weaker fallback — no shared-copy web-mirror files exist in the final diff.

FF-1's denylist item 'обратных кавычек с ${' (backtick-with-interpolation) as a literal blanket ban produced false positives against every ordinary error-message string the new formula-*.ts files legitimately build (e.g. a template literal like `formula references unknown field "${ast.field}"`). Narrowed the bash-check's actual grep pattern to the injection-relevant shape only — a template literal IMMEDIATELY INVOKED as a function (the real template-tag-abuse vector, e.g. `` `...`() ``) — while every other FF-1 token (eval(/new Function/Function(/require(/import(/vm/process./globalThis/__proto__/child_process/constructor.constructor) is unchanged from the ADR spec. Documented the narrowing in the check's header comment; added both a positive self-test (the narrowed pattern still fires on a genuine invoked-template sample) and a negative self-test (an ordinary message-building template literal does NOT false-positive) so the narrowing itself is provably correct, not just asserted.
friction_events: FE-T0580-1: root node_modules and web/node_modules were both fully absent in the freshly provisioned worktree (not merely a stale lockfile) — ran `npm install` in both directories to obtain vitest/tsc/eslint/vite binaries. package-lock.json in both places verified BYTE-IDENTICAL after install via `git status --short` (clean on both).

FE-T0580-2: the ADR's literally-worded preferred web-core-import pattern does not resolve under this repo's toolchain (see deviations_from_adr above for the full explanation) — the working alternative (explicit `.ts` extension on the specifier) was discovered by reading an existing test file's own import line rather than guessing, then verified against both the vitest runner and a real `vite build` before committing to it.

FE-T0580-3: PUT /api/registry-defs/:id resolves its DB pool (crudDeps.pool ?? poolHint ?? a lazy singleton that throws 503 without DATABASE_URL) BEFORE any request-body validation runs (pre-existing code order, unrelated to this task) — the new HTTP-level formula-gate unit tests for PUT needed an injected `poolHint` (a stub pool wired to throw if ever queried) to avoid a spurious 503 masking the 400 the formula gate is supposed to produce; using a throw-on-use stub also PROVED (rather than merely asserted) that the gate rejects an invalid formula before any real DB query is attempted.
